title: Mexican Breakfast Roasted Pork and Chile Hash
summary: This vibrant Mexican breakfast roast brings bold morning flavors to your table with roasted pork shoulder seasoned with traditional spices. Accentuated by smoky roasted chilies and fresh herbs, this dish transforms a classic weekend feast into a hearty morning masterpiece. The long roasting process develops deep caramelized notes while keeping the interior remarkably tender and juicy. Paired with warm handmade tortillas, scrambled eggs, and pickled red onions, it provides a satisfying balance of rich savory goodness and bright acidic tang. Crisp radishes, creamy avocado slices, and crumbled cotija cheese add contrasting textures that elevate every bite. Ideal for a slow Sunday family brunch, this recipe scales easily to feed a crowd while filling your home with intoxicating aromas of toasted cumin, oregano, and sweet charred garlic. Enjoy this comforting creation alongside chilled hibiscus tea or rich cinnamon coffee for a memorable breakfast experience. Every single element is designed to harmonize beautifully on the plate.

steps.step: Carefully measure and trim the excess fat from the pork shoulder before placing it on a heavy wooden cutting board.
Dice the trimmed pork shoulder into uniform two-inch cubes to ensure even cooking throughout the roasting process.
Combine the ground cumin, dried oregano, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder inside a small mixing bowl.
Add two teaspoons of sea salt and one teaspoon of freshly cracked black pepper to the fragrant dry seasoning mix.
Stir the dry spice blend thoroughly with a small whisk until all components are evenly distributed throughout.
Mince the four cloves of fresh garlic finely using a sharp chef knife on a dedicated garlic cutting board.
Dice the large red onion into small clean pieces and set them aside in a stainless steel prep container.
Slice the yellow onion into neat matching pieces and store them alongside the cut red onions for later cooking.
Scrub the russet potatoes thoroughly under cold running tap water to remove any surface dirt and debris.
Peel the russet potatoes completely before dicing them into crisp half-inch cubes for the hearty roast hash.
Scrub and peel the sweet potatoes carefully using a sharp vegetable peeler over the kitchen sink basin.
Dice the sweet potatoes into uniform cubes matching the size of the russet potato pieces for balanced roasting.
Deseed the poblano peppers completely and cut them into thin even strips on a sturdy prep chopping board.
Slice the jalapeno peppers into fine dice while wearing gloves to protect your hands from spicy chili oils.
Chop the fresh cilantro finely and place it into a small serving bowl ready for the final garnish step.
Juice the fresh limes until you collect one quarter cup of tart citrus liquid for brightening the meat.
Measure the chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, and agave nectar into a glass measuring cup for liquid roasting.
Place the cubed pork shoulder into a very large stainless steel mixing bowl to begin the seasoning stage.
Pour the prepared dry spice mixture generously over all sides of the raw cubed pork shoulder inside the bowl.
Add the minced garlic and sliced green onions to the spice-covered pork shoulder cubes in the mixing bowl.
Drizzle two tablespoons of olive oil over the seasoned pork shoulder pieces to help the spices stick well.
Use clean hands to massage the rub thoroughly into every cut surface of the pork shoulder until fully coated.
Cover the mixing bowl tightly with plastic wrap to trap the rich herbal aromas during the short marinating time.
Let the seasoned pork rest at cool room temperature for twenty minutes while preheating the heavy oven pan.
Preheat your main roasting oven to three hundred seventy five degrees Fahrenheit for optimal meat roasting.
Prepare a large heavy Dutch oven by wiping the interior dry with a clean paper towel before heating.
Add one tablespoon of lard to the dry Dutch oven and place it over medium-high stove heat until fully melted.
Verify that the lard is shimmering and hot across the entire bottom surface of the heavy metal vessel.
Uncover the marinated pork shoulder cubes and give them one final stir to reapply any fallen spices.
Scatter the ground coriander and chipotle powder over the pork pieces for an extra layer of bold flavor.
Mix the additional spices thoroughly into the pork shoulder cubes using a sturdy silicone spatula.
Set aside two tablespoons of the spice blend for dusting over the roasted vegetables in a later phase.
Verify the oven has reached three hundred seventy five degrees before proceeding to the searing sequence.
Organize your cooking tongs and splat guards near the stovetop for safe and efficient pan sear handling.
Carefully lay half of the seasoned pork shoulder cubes into the hot shimmering lard inside the Dutch oven.
Sear the pork cubes without moving them for three minutes until a deep golden brown crust forms underneath.
Turn each pork cube carefully using metal tongs to brown all remaining sides evenly in the hot vessel.
Transfer the first batch of seared pork cubes onto a clean rimmed baking sheet using a slotted spoon.
Add the remaining vegetable oil to the Dutch oven and allow it to warm up for thirty seconds over heat.
Place the second batch of seasoned pork shoulder cubes into the hot pot in a single uncrowded layer.
Sear this second batch for three minutes per side until properly caramelized and beautifully browned all over.
Remove the second batch of pork shoulder from the Dutch oven and set it aside with the first seared batch.
Reduce the stovetop burner heat to medium to prevent burning the rendered pan drippings and fond.
Add the diced red onions and yellow onions directly into the hot fat remaining inside the Dutch oven.
Sauté the onion mixture for four minutes while scraping the brown browned bits from the pot bottom.
Add the sliced poblano peppers and diced jalapenos to the sautéed onions inside the heavy Dutch oven.
Cook the pepper and onion mix for three minutes until slightly softened and wonderfully fragrant throughout.
Stir in the diced russet and sweet potato cubes to combine them with the sautéed aromatic vegetables.
Dust the potato and pepper mixture with the reserved spice blend and stir well for two full minutes.
Return all of the seared pork shoulder cubes and accumulated juices back into the heavy Dutch oven.
Pour the chicken broth and lime juice over the ingredients and stir gently with a wooden spoon.
Tuck the two dried bay leaves deep into the center of the liquid and pork mixture inside the Dutch oven.
Cover the Dutch oven tightly with its heavy lid to seal in all essential moisture and roasting steam.
Carefully transfer the covered Dutch oven onto the middle rack of your preheated three hundred seventy five oven.
Roast the pork and vegetable hash covered for forty five minutes to tenderize the meat and root vegetables.
Carefully remove the lid using heavy oven mitts to allow the surface liquid to evaporate and brown.
Continue roasting uncovered for an additional twenty minutes until the pork edges turn crispy and caramelized.
Check the tenderness of the pork cubes by piercing a larger piece with a sharp metal kitchen fork.
Verify that the potato cubes are tender all the way through without becoming mushy or falling apart entirely.
Remove the heavy Dutch oven carefully from the hot oven and place it onto a heatproof trivet on the counter.
Discard the two dried bay leaves carefully using metal kitchen tongs and discard them into compost.
Drizzle the apple cider vinegar and agave nectar over the hot roasted hash to balance the deep savory notes.
Gently stir the roasted hash from the bottom up to distribute the rich pan reduced juices evenly.
Taste a small piece of potato and adjust seasoning with a pinch of sea salt if needed for best flavor.
Cover the pot loosely with aluminum foil to keep the roasted hash piping hot while cooking the breakfast eggs.
Set a large nonstick skillet onto the stovetop burner over medium-low heat to prepare for egg frying.
Melt one tablespoon of unsalted butter across the entire bottom surface of the warm nonstick skillet.
Crack six large fresh eggs into individual small glass ramekins to ensure easy pouring without shell fragments.
Gently slide the cracked eggs into the warm buttered nonstick skillet one at a time with low heat.
Season the cooking eggs lightly with a small pinch of sea salt and cracked black pepper for taste.
Fry the eggs gently on medium-low heat for three minutes until the whites are fully set but yolks remain runny.
Optionally flip the eggs carefully if over-medium texture is preferred by your breakfast guests.
Remove the nonstick skillet from heat source as soon as whites solidify to prevent overcooking the yolks.
Warm six small corn tortillas over an open gas flame for ten seconds per side until soft and pliable.
Wrap the warmed corn tortillas in a clean cloth kitchen towel to keep them moist, warm, and flexible.
Slice one fresh avocado in half, remove the pit safely, and cut into neat decorative fan slices.
Crumble the cotija cheese into fine uniform crumbs using your fingers into a small condiment bowl.
Slice fresh red radishes paper-thin using a sharp mandoline slicer for a crisp colorful topping layer.
Organize the pickled jalapeno slices, sour cream, and tomatillo salsa on the serving table station.
Spoon a generous portion of hot roasted pork and vegetable hash onto six broad warm dinner plates.
Top each serving of roasted hash carefully with one perfectly fried egg using a wide silicone spatula.
Arrange avocado slices and thin radish rounds neatly alongside the fried egg on each serving plate.
Sprinkle crumbled cotija cheese and fresh chopped cilantro over the top of each completed breakfast dish.
Add a spoonful of tomatillo salsa beside the egg on each plate for a bright green color accent.
Dollop a small tablespoon of fresh sour cream onto the edge of each warm hash plate for rich contrast.
Scatter pickled jalapeno slices across the top to provide an inviting spicy crunch to every serving.
Serve two warm corn tortillas alongside each plate tucked neatly under the edge of the dish.
Dust a tiny pinch of chipotle powder over the egg yolks for an attractive finished presentation style.
Place fresh lime wedges on the side of each plate for guests to squeeze over their food as desired.
Inspect each completed plate to ensure all colorful garnishes are neatly positioned and visually appealing.
Serve the hot Mexican breakfast roast immediately while the eggs remain warm and yolks perfectly runny.
Provide extra salsa, sour cream, and warm tortillas at the table for guests who desire larger portions.
Pair this rich dish with hot cinnamon coffee or cold hibiscus tea for a complete traditional meal.
Offer fresh hot sauce at the table so individuals can adjust heat levels according to personal tastes.
Clear prep utensils away from the dining area to maintain a clean and enjoyable breakfast environment.
Store any leftover roast hash in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to three full days.
Reheat leftovers in a hot skillet with a splash of water to restore moisture before serving again.
Fry fresh eggs when serving leftover hash to ensure the best texture and taste experience possible.
Enjoy this comforting homemade Mexican breakfast feast surrounded by family and good morning cheer.
